entry_conditions: Accept supported entries anywhere in the full expanded transition, not only transport. Supply two consecutive 20 Hz raw world-frame observations: qpos[0:9] including per-finger aperture in metres, qvel[9:18], TCP pose[18:25], red/blue poses[25:39], and goals[41:47]. Joint angles are radians and pose quaternions are wxyz. Open low approach, imminent closure, partial lift, elevated carry and moving entries are represented. demo10000/80 has TCP z about 0.066 m and open fingers; /107 issues close while fingers are still open; /150 is partially lifted. The learned two-step recurrent posterior, not a forced transport initialization, selects event/progress. Keep carried/next role IDs in orchestration, but this fixed model interface cannot consume them or past commands: it reconstructs the observed red-then-blue roles and command persistence from state. If history is unavailable duplicate the latest state, with uncalibrated confidence; truncated-history training is not a guarantee.
exit_conditions: A useful nonterminal late exit is open empty retreat or high approach to the next block while the delivered block rests near its goal. The delivered object should remain separated from the rising/moving TCP, and measured finger opening should agree with the inferred phase. demo10001/417 is still moving at TCP z about 0.268 m, with red at about 0.020 m and each finger about 0.040 m; nonzero qvel is supported. A terminal continuation can reach nearly stationary open retreat as at demo10011/777, TCP z about 0.299 m and both blocks at about 0.020 m. These are skill readiness cues, not extra task-success requirements. Evaluate the supplied single-observation rotated XY containment and z-tolerance contract separately; release, clearance, speed and sustained hold are not required for task success.
overlap_role: Train and execute over all assigned expanded slices without trimming shared phases. Incoming overlaps, for example demo10000 [80,185) and [470,585), cover open approach, command closure, aperture response, lift and initial horizontal motion. Outgoing overlap [265,425) begins with the red block still held and descending, then includes release lag, dwell, retreat and high blue approach. Corresponding demo10001 overlaps are [78,185), [260,417), [463,580); demo10011 overlaps are [84,192), [272,435), [480,584). Learned phase-progress clocks and action knots support event-conditioned continuation at different observed starts, not switching at a fixed episode timestamp. The red role is retained through the high next approach in this model's training semantics.
successor_readiness: Transfer the live two-observation history, current object/goal poses, actual apertures and qvel, plus stable carried/next role IDs in the caller. Supply past executed commands to a successor if its interface supports them; this model does not. The successor must be capable of predecessor completion if invoked early in the shared descending/releasing interval, rather than assuming an already empty approach. A geometric placement may already hold while fingers remain around the object: demo10000/290 has red z about 0.0226 m and closed fingers, while /305 is nearly the same arm pose but fingers about 0.03976 m. Raw state evidence outranks a high latent phase index. A terminal no-next-object indication and the measured one-observation task-contract result should remain separate from latent event completion.
failure_signatures: Release prediction while a block is still elevated, reopening during transport, returning to pickup after placement, role switching merely because red reaches the pad while still held, or endlessly dwelling despite observed opening/separation indicate a poor temporal belief. demo10000/691-/693 shows physical opening over multiple observations, so a changed command alone is not evidence of disengagement. Slow target tracking can resemble a dwell; tiny measured velocities may carry expert timing and are not proof of elapsed progress. Do not reject all moving entries or impose near-zero qvel at transfer. There is no trained retry graph, calibrated timeout or certified recovery for a missed grasp.
continuation_guidance: Reobserve after the framework's executed prefix (8 actions at 20 Hz), then infer a fresh event posterior and remaining durations from the causal pair. Continue this policy when the successor cannot complete the ongoing low approach/lift or descent/release, or when smooth open retreat is desired. Transfer within the shared overlap when the successor can reconstruct predecessor completion from measured state and roles. Stop or transfer based on caller needs and the supplied task contract, not a fixed elapsed duration or phase number. If task success is reached before opening or clearance, the caller may stop immediately under the contract, or choose learned open-retreat continuation. No low-level scripted switch or termination gate is implemented.
limitations: Observed support comes from successful red-then-blue demonstrations, not recovery trials. Aperture near 0.0183 m and TCP/object co-motion are inferred grasp evidence, not a contact sensor. State-only two-frame recurrence cannot always distinguish identical dwell states and cannot accept an arbitrary nominated role absent from the interface. The actual executable prior uses local soft event labels, geometric progress, censored duration supervision, learned progress-domain denoiser resampling and a separate persistent gripper reference; it does not possess full offline phase clocks or executed-command memory. Phase and duration uncertainty are not asserted calibrated. There is no IK/FK, image model, invariance, hard placement constraint, collision guarantee or empirical rollout-performance claim. Shared complete-original-data normalization is preserved.
